name: Lewis-Sumner Syndrome
aliases: Multifocal Acquired Demyelinating Sensory and Motor Neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: EFNS/PNS Diagnostic Criteria for Lewis-Sumner Syndrome

criteria.description: Multifocal demyelinating neuropathy affecting motor and sensory nerves with conduction block on electrophysiological studies
Asymmetric, multifocal weakness and sensory loss predominantly in upper limbs
Mild to moderate elevation of cerebrospinal fluid protein without pleocytosis
Clinical improvement or stabilization with immunomodulatory treatment such as IVIG or steroids

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multifocal demyelinating neuropathy with conduction block plus compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other demyelinating neuropathies such as CIDP and multifocal motor neuropathy.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multifocal conduction block on nerve conduction studies
searchTerms: multiple nerve signal blocks on tests
uneven weakness in hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multifocal sensory loss with predominant involvement of upper limbs
searchTerms: patchy loss of sensation mainly in arms
multifocal sensory deficits in upper limbs
uneven numbness in hands and arms
muscle wasting in arms or legs

common.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in affected limbs

searchTerms: tingling or numbness in affected areas

common.symptomName: Mild distal limb pain or dysesthesia
searchTerms: mild pain or abnormal feelings in hands and feet
slight burning or tingling in limbs
problems with eye or face movement
weakness in upper arm and thigh muscles

occasional.symptomName: Mild gait disturbance due to distal weakness
searchTerms: slight walking problems due to weak feet and hands
mild unsteady gait from distal weakness
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Elevated CSF protein with normal cell count (albuminocytologic dissociation)
imaging: MRI may show nerve root or plexus hypertrophy
Nerve ultrasound may reveal multifocal nerve enlargement
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations; considered an acquired immune-mediated neuropathy
other: Electrophysiological studies demonstrating multifocal conduction block and demyelination

distinguishingFeatures: More uniform demyelination without multifocal conduction block
Purely motor involvement without sensory deficits

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over days
references: Lewis RA, Sumner AJ. Multifocal acquired demyelinating sensory and motor neuropathy. Brain. 1982.
EFNS/PNS guidelines on diagnosis and treatment of chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. J Peripher Nerv Syst. 2010.
Dalakas MC. Multifocal acquired demyelinating sensory and motor neuropathy: clinical and immunopathological features. Neurology. 1994.
